Bottle baby Velcro had no idea today was the day. One minute he’s happily slurping a bottle, the next, he’s in Cadence’s arms for his wethering. And before you think we’re being mean, here’s the truth — this is one of the kindest choices we can make for him and our herd. Wethering (neutering a male goat) helps prevent aggressive behavior, dangerous horns, and the constant urge to challenge every fence, bucket, and human that crosses his path. It also means he’ll live a calmer, longer, healthier life without the stress of breeding hormones running the show. For us as ranchers, it’s about balance. We can’t keep every buck intact that would lead to overbreeding, inbreeding, overpopulation, and unhealthy competition. By wethering, we make sure only the best genetics are passed on while the rest of the boys get to live happy, peaceful lives as pasture buddies, brush clearers, and professional cud-chewers. Velcro will be back to bouncing around the pasture by tomorrow, bottle in mouth, tail wagging. He won’t remember today, but it’ll make all the difference for his future. #GoatTok #BottleBabyGoat #Wethering #FarmLife #GoatLife #GoatCare #AnimalHusbandry #HomesteadLife #HappyGoats #KikoGoats #GoatFarm #PastureRaised

The Arctic Fox (Vulpes lagopus), sometimes called the snow fox, is a small but remarkably hardy fox adapted to some of the coldest environments on Earth. Its thick fur changes with the seasons white during winter to blend into snow and brown or grey in summer to camouflage against rocks and vegetation. Its compact body, short ears, and furry paws help conserve heat in freezing conditions. Arctic foxes are symbols of adaptability, resilience, intelligence, and survival. They inhabit Arctic tundra across the Northern Hemisphere and can withstand temperatures far below freezing while searching for rodents, birds, eggs, fish, and carrion. Fun fact: An Arctic fox can survive temperatures approaching −50°C (−58°F), partly because its thick winter coat provides exceptional insulation. #ArcticFox #SnowFox #VulpesLagopus #Wildlife #Winter
